headline: Disney+ partners with TikTok to bring fan-made shorts using Marvel, Star Wars IP
summary: The collaboration grants US-based creators official access to a vast library of Disney assets for hundreds of films and series, including Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars, for videos hosted on both platforms.
details: Disney and TikTok have penned a deal to bring Disney-centric vertical videos to Disney+'s Verts section. This partnership grants creators access to a deep library of Disney assets for their videos.
The initially US-only pilot allows approved creators to use IP from Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars. Their videos will be hosted on both TikTok and in Verts on Disney+.
These fan-generated videos will be regularly refreshed to engage subscribers and grow the audience. Disney and TikTok are also launching a Creator Ambassador Program to nurture top creators.
Disney's investment is driven by TikTok data, showing 6.5 million daily film/TV posts last year. A survey revealed half of respondents were inspired to watch content by TikTok videos.
The collaboration will launch as a pilot in the coming months, with no firm date announced. This follows recent reports about Disney potentially planning a free tier for Disney+.
caption:
TikTok creators can now officially use Marvel, Star Wars, and Pixar IP for videos on Disney+.

Disney and TikTok have penned a deal to bring Disney-centric vertical videos to Disney+'s Verts section. This partnership grants creators access to a deep library of Disney assets for their videos.

The initially US-only pilot allows approved creators to use IP from Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars. Their videos will be hosted on both TikTok and in Verts on Disney+.

These fan-generated videos will be regularly refreshed to engage subscribers and grow the audience. Disney and TikTok are also launching a Creator Ambassador Program to nurture top creators.

Disney's investment is driven by TikTok data, showing 6.5 million daily film/TV posts last year. A survey revealed half of respondents were inspired to watch content by TikTok videos.

The collaboration will launch as a pilot in the coming months, with no firm date announced. This follows recent reports about Disney potentially planning a free tier for Disney+.

Source: Engadget, TechCrunch, The Verge

headline_marked: [[YouTube outlines AI content monetization rules]], restricting payment for 'inauthentic' videos
headline: YouTube outlines AI content monetization rules, restricting payment for 'inauthentic' videos
summary: The platform is updating its Partner Program policies, shifting focus from 'repetitious' to 'inauthentic' content to ensure effort and creativity, even with AI tools.
details: YouTube has clarified its policy on AI-generated videos, stating that while they are allowed, certain types of 'inauthentic content' will not be eligible for monetization through the YouTube Partner Program (YPP). This move comes as AI-generated videos, or 'slop,' have become increasingly prevalent on the platform.

The policy change redefines 'repetitious content' as 'inauthentic content,' emphasizing that creators, even those using AI, must demonstrate effort and creativity. This is not a blanket ban on generative AI, but rather a guide for creators to understand what is required to monetize their videos.

Three specific categories of AI content are explicitly banned from monetization: generic and repetitive videos (often content farming), off-putting or distressing content (like animals in peril), and 'AI personas' offering advice on serious topics such as finance.

These new rules are distinct from YouTube's general community guidelines, which prohibit content like nudity or hate speech. The updated YPP policies specifically target the quality and authenticity of AI-generated videos for monetization purposes.

Despite YouTube's introduction of automatic AI detection, some AI-generated videos may still evade detection due to advancing technology. Users can look for clues like video length (shorter clips often hide AI errors better) or intentionally low-quality visuals.

Other telltale signs of AI include hyper-realistic visuals with perfectly coiffed hair and symmetrical faces that seem out of context, or subtle errors in physics, perspective, and reflections. These inconsistencies can help viewers spot AI-generated content.
